subject: Re: Data retention/deletion SLAs - backups & logs
messages:
From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>

Subject: Post-call: Data retention & deletion SLAs (summary + next steps)

Hi Jorge / Amaya Security Team,

Thanks again for the time on the call this morning - appreciated the thoughtful questions. Per our discussion, I wanted to summarize the current Redwood positions and propose concrete next steps so your security & compliance reviewers have what they need.

Key items we discussed:
- SOC 2: We maintain a SOC 2 control program and can provide our most recent SOC 2 summary and scope under an NDA / secure share (Marissa can follow up with the report access).
- GDPR / Data subject requests: We support standard DSAR workflows and can mark and purge user data on request; details below.
- Deletion SLAs: application-level deletion (logical) completed within 24 hours of request. Physical removal from primary (hot) stores occurs within 30 days; backups are addressed separately.
- Logs & analytics: Event logs retained for 90 days by default; longer retention can be configured via contract for enterprise customers.
- Backups: Incremental backups are retained for up to 12 months. Because backups are immutable, deletion of backup copies follows a documented workflow and may require up to 30 days to complete once deletion is triggered.

Requested items from Amaya:
1) Please confirm whether you require customer-managed encryption keys (CMKs) for this project.
2) Any specific maximum retention for logs or backups (we default to 90 days / 12 months).
3) Please complete the attached vendor security questionnaire and we'll address any gaps.

Attachments: redwood_data_retention_matrix.xlsx (retention matrix + notes)

Next steps / owner:
- Jorge: share completed security questionnaire (security@amaya.com) - target Wed 8/12
- Marissa: share SOC 2 access and any redacted evidence - Marissa will follow up
- Rishi: join any technical deep-dive if needed (backup/deletion mechanics)

If helpful, we can schedule a 30-min follow-up with Rishi and Marissa later this week.

Thanks,
Neha Kapoor

Redwood Inference

Hi Neha,

Thanks for the clear summary. A couple of clarifying questions from our security team:

1) Customer-managed keys: we prefer CMK for production; do you support CMK in the Private deployment / VPC option? If not, what controls around key rotation and access do you provide?
2) Deletion SLA expectations: can you clarify the difference between logical deletion and physical deletion? For compliance we prefer a committed maximum for total removal (including backups) - is the 30 days you mentioned the guaranteed maximum?
3) Backups: are backups encrypted at rest with unique keys per-tenant? How do you handle backups for dedicated pools vs. hosted?

I've attached our vendor security questionnaire; please have your security team complete the sections related to data retention, backup, and incident response.

Attachment: Amaya_Security_Questionnaire.pdf

Happy to set up a short meeting with our security engineer if that helps.

Best,
Jorge Lopez
Head of IT & Security
Amaya Health
jorge.lopez@amaya.com

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jorge Lopez <jorge.lopez@amaya.com>, Amaya Security Team <security@amaya.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 11 Aug 2026 09:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: Data retention & deletion SLAs (summary + next steps)

Hi Jorge - thanks for the questions, happy to clarify. Short answers up front, details below.

- CMK: Yes, we support customer-managed keys for our Private deployment and Dedicated offerings; for hosted tenants we offer BYOK in select regions. We can detail key management in the security questionnaire.
- Deletion SLA: Logical/application deletion: typically completed within 24 hours. Physical removal from primary stores: <= 30 days. For backups, because snapshots are immutable, we commit to marking the data for removal and purging it from backup rotation within 30 days after the deletion request is processed; depending on backup windows the actual removal may take up to 60 days in extreme cases - we document the process and can provide timeline guarantees in contract language if needed.
- Encryption: All backups are encrypted at rest. For Dedicated and Private customers we can enable tenant-specific keys; hosted uses system-managed keys unless BYOK is added.
- SOC 2: Redwood maintains SOC 2 controls; Type II report is available for in-scope customers under an NDA. I will start the access process and send a secure link for download.

Below is a short mapping from your asks to how we meet them: 
- Data subject deletion (GDPR): we provide an API for DSARs and a documented purge workflow.
- Audit logs: retained 90 days by default; extended retention can be added as a paid option or contract deliverable.
- Backups & restores: incremental daily snapshots + monthly full snapshot; retention default 12 months; deletion requires coordination due to immutability/retention windows.

I've partially completed the attached questionnaire and left a few technical notes for Rishi to handle (backup/restore internals). Please see the redwood_data_retention_matrix.xlsx for specifics (column notes on SLA, backup windows, and key options).

If you want contractual language for deletion SLAs we can propose the following: application-level deletion within 24 hours, physical removal from active stores within 30 days, and backup purging within 60 days from request date (with the option to shorten if needed and included in the contract). Let me know if you need tighter wording and I will loop in Legal.

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Director, Security & Trust Ops
Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com
